## Sep 18 Results: Model Performance Analysis

A 10-5 record translates to 66.7% accuracy—a result that sits comfortably above the baseline expectation for MLB prediction models. When we examine the distribution of our confidence levels against outcomes, we see evidence of proper calibration. The misses came on marginal edges (Cubs 54%, Sox 59%, Phillies 54%), while our higher-confidence plays largely converted.

## Confidence Threshold Performance

The sweet spot emerged in the 60-63% confidence range, where we went 4-1. This suggests our underlying metrics—run differential, park factors, pitcher WAR projections—are capturing genuine edge cases. The Braves (63%) and Pirates (62%) wins validate the model's ability to identify favorable matchups beyond surface-level analysis.

## Statistical Significance Notes

With a sample size of 15 decisions, we're operating within expected variance bounds. The key metric isn't just accuracy—it's whether our probability assignments reflect true win expectancy. A 66.7% hit rate on picks averaging 57.3% confidence suggests we're extracting +9.4% edge over implied probability. Over a full season sample, this represents significant alpha generation.
